title: A portal's glass shows its destination through a window that parallaxes with the viewer's eye, and a pick through it lands on the destination's surface
binding: The positive leg boots an offscreen 256x144 world whose one placement, a door, has a glass face carrying a portal facet (destination 'beyond', arrival mapped onto the destination's 'arch/glass' counterpart) and showing a session of that same destination with the window projection. The destination (beyond.world.json) is a persisted global world holding an arch at the door's position facing it, a green emissive marker of radius one half six units behind the arch, and a blue emissive backdrop twelve units behind it. A fixed camera looks at the door from six units back, and the seat's body stands nine units back, behind the camera, so its eye fits the window without entering the frame. world.screens lists the glass as screen 24 showing session:beyond, bound, its mapping naming the session instance over the glass (0.96x0.8 half extents, proud of the face at z 0.1) at the session's 144x120 extent, with no bezel warp. The body steps a unit right of the door and the captured frame shows the marker right of the glass's centre against the blue backdrop, with the glass left of centre blue; it steps a unit left and the marker shows left of centre, with the glass right of centre blue, so the window reframes the destination from the viewer's eye. With the view at three-quarter scale, a display point on the marker's image walks through the room's view onto the glass (session$24's pixel 43,58), through the camera the window rendered into the destination's world, and lands on the marker's near surface at 0.02,1.47,-5.5; a point beside it lands on the backdrop at 1.4,1.42,-11.9. The discriminating leg shows a window onto a different destination (elsewhere.world.json: the same arch before a red backdrop and no marker): the screen lists session:elsewhere, both marker observations and both blue observations turn red, and the pick on the marker's image lands on the red backdrop instead, while the pick beside it lands on the same point of the backdrop in both legs, which shows the walk runs the same way through either window.
